title: Bottled water for 3 days (3 litres per person per day)
description: Maintain at least 3 litres of bottled potable water per person per day for drinking (9 litres per person for 3 days). More is needed for basic food rehydration, cooking, and hygiene.
tip: Commercially sealed bottled water retains potable quality for years if unopened. Keep large 5L bottles for home and 2L/500ml bottles for grab bags.

title: Non-perishable food for 3 days (ambient rolling pantry)
description: Stock 3 days of food with a long shelf life that doesn't need refrigeration or cooking: tinned meat, fish, beans, vegetables, dried fruit and nuts, pasta, and rolled oats. It's best to buy food you'd usually eat.
tip: Ensure you possess a manual tin opener. Without one, tinned provisions are inaccessible during electrical outages.

title: Torch (and spare batteries) & LED lanterns
description: Place reliable battery-powered LED torches, head torches, and lanterns on each floor of your home, plus sealed spare alkaline batteries. Strictly avoid candles or open flames due to documented fire risks.
tip: Head torches leave both hands free for cooking, attending to family members, or examining utility stopcocks.

title: Blankets, sleeping bags and warm clothing
description: Keep warm blankets, thermal layers, 3-season sleeping bags, wool hats, and thick socks readily accessible for each household member in case of winter power cuts or central heating boiler collapse.
tip: Dress in multiple loose, warm layers rather than one thick garment. Keep emergency thermal foil blankets in your grab bags.

title: FM radio (battery / wind-up)
description: Maintain an analogue FM/AM or wind-up broadcast radio with spare batteries. National broadcasters (notably BBC Radio 4 on 92.4–94.6 MHz FM) are the statutory conduit for civil contingency emergency directives when cellular masts lose power.
tip: Test reception of BBC Radio 4 and local BBC stations twice per year to verify frequency familiarity.

title: Charged portable power bank
description: Retain at least one high-capacity portable power bank (10,000 to 20,000 mAh) fully charged at all times to recharge mobile phones, torches, or medical equipment during power cuts.
tip: Top up power banks on the first weekend of every month to counteract natural chemical self-discharge.

title: Cash (mix of coins and notes) & payment cards
description: Keep physical cash in a mix of small banknotes (£5, £10, £20) and coins for vending/payphones/convenience shops, as electronic card terminals fail during power cuts or telecom throttles. Also retain physical payment cards with chip & PIN.
tip: Avoid £50 notes as convenience stores and pharmacies may be unable to provide change during network outages.

title: Copies of IDs and vital documents
description: Store certified physical photocopies of passports, photo driving licences, birth certificates, home/car insurance policies, and essential contracts in a portable waterproof pouch.
tip: Include an unencrypted USB memory drive with high-resolution digital scans stored inside the pouch.

title: Important phone numbers & medical information card
description: Carry a durable card listing immediate family mobile numbers, an agreed out-of-area relative contact point, primary meeting points, regular medication and dosages. If possible laminate cards.
tip: When cellular towers saturate, out-of-area trunk lines and SMS text messages succeed when local voice calls fail. If possible laminate cards so they remain legible in wet weather.

title: First aid items & basic medicine kit
description: Equip your home with sterile dressings, adhesive bandages/plasters, antiseptic wipes, burn dressings, medical tape, trauma shears, and non-prescription pain relief medication (paracetamol, ibuprofen, antihistamines).
tip: Keep the first aid kit in a central location known to all adults and older children.

title: Essential medication and medical supplies
description: Ensure family members dependent on critical daily prescription medicines maintain a rolling 14 to 30 day supply, reordering repeat prescriptions well before final doses with paper dosage notes.
tip: Store a printed copy of repeat prescription slips listing specific medication names, dosages, and GP surgery contacts.

title: Hand sanitiser, wet wipes, hygiene & bathroom products
description: Stock antibacterial hand sanitiser, wet wipes, toilet tissue, toothbrushes, toothpaste, bar soap, feminine sanitary products, and heavy-duty refuse sacks for household hygiene when mains water pressure drops.
tip: Wet wipes and alcohol hand rub provide effective personal hygiene without consuming limited drinking water supplies.

title: Baby formula (ready-to-feed), nappies & wipes
description: For households with infants: ready-made or 'ready-to-feed' liquid formula bottles are best, as you may not be able to boil water safely to make up powdered formula. Keep a 3-day supply of nappies, wipes, and nappy sacks. (Mark as Not Applicable if household has no infants).
tip: Powdered formula demands boiled potable water at 70°C to kill bacteria; liquid formula bottles remain completely sterile and ready at room temperature without power.

title: Pet food and bottled water for 3 days
description: For households with animals: maintain 3 to 5 days of wet and dry pet food, dedicated pet drinking water (1.5 litres per day per medium animal), bowls, medication, and pet waste bags. (Mark as Not Applicable if household has no pets).
tip: Pets must not consume unboiled or contaminated floodwater; allocate their water reserve alongside human stores.

title: Locate and tag household utility shutoffs (Stopcock, Breakers, Gas)
description: Ensure all adult household members know the precise location of the internal stopcock (water), gas meter isolation lever, and electricity consumer unit (main breaker). If possible laminate cards and affix beside meters.
tip: Affix a durable tag to the water stopcock and test turning it quarterly to prevent limescale seizure.

title: Connect with your community & swap contact details
description: Talk to your neighbours about what extra support you might be able to share during an outage, and swap contact details. Check on elderly or vulnerable residents nearby, and help by photocopying or printing important documents for them.
tip: Community mutual aid is often the fastest support available during localized infrastructure outages. Donate surplus items if you have extra provisions.

title: Six-month kit check & expiry date review
description: Set a recurring reminder every six months to check expiry dates on food, water, and medicines, swap out items that need replacing, and update your kit if your household's needs have changed.
tip: Align your biannual kit check with the daylight saving clock changes in spring and autumn.

title: Maintain vehicle fuel tank at least half-full
description: Adopt the discipline of refuelling when your fuel tank dips to half capacity. Petrol forecourt pumps rely on grid electricity; during a blackout, stations cannot dispense fuel.
tip: In winter, keep a warm blanket, sturdy footwear, and a bottle of water in the boot.

title: One-month extended food reserve with rotation plan
description: Build a supplementary 30-day reserve of long-life staples (bulk oats, pulses, tinned meat/fish, vacuum-sealed grains, dried soups) tailored to your household's dietary and caloric requirements.
tip: Label cartons with month/year of acquisition and rotate items into your weekly cooking to ensure zero waste.

title: Gravity water filtration or certified microfiltration
description: Possess a gravity-fed ceramic/carbon filter (e.g. British Berkefeld, Doulton) or hollow-fibre membrane filter (0.1 micron) to purify municipal bowser water or rainwater safely.
tip: Certified 0.1-micron filters remove 99.999% of bacteria, cysts, and protozoa without chemical tablets.

title: Solar battery charger or portable power station
description: Deploy a foldable solar panel (30W-100W) paired with a portable LiFePO4 battery power station (250Wh-1000Wh) for sustaining phones, radios, lanterns, or essential medical diagnostic devices.
tip: Solar should supplement, never replace, pre-charged power banks. In UK winter weather, solar output can drop to 10-15% of rated capacity. For CPAP or medical devices, verify power station watt-hour requirements in advance.
buyingGuidance: Use case guidance: (1) Small 30W folding panel for phones/head torches in summer; (2) 500Wh portable power station for low-draw lighting, routers, and medical kit; (3) Do not rely on pocket solar chargers with tiny internal batteries as they charge too slowly under British cloud cover.

title: Safe fuel reserve in approved jerry cans
description: Store up to 20 litres of petrol or diesel in UK HSE-approved metal (Wavian) or certified HDPE plastic containers in a well-ventilated outbuilding or secure garage away from living quarters.
tip: Under UK Petroleum Regulations, storing more than 30 litres of petrol at home requires licensing. Add a quality fuel stabiliser to prevent petrol degradation over six months.

title: Trauma haemorrhage kit and basic first aid training
description: Equip an emergency trauma pack including a certified windlass tourniquet (CAT Gen 7), haemostatic gauze (Celox / QuikClot), emergency pressure bandages, and burn dressings. Complete a recognized St John Ambulance or British Red Cross course.
tip: Tourniquets and haemostatic dressings save lives within minutes during severe cuts or structural collapses before blue-light services arrive.

title: Off-grid communications (PMR446 radios / Satellite)
description: Keep a pair of licence-free PMR446 two-way walkie-talkies for local neighbourhood contact up to 1-3km, or a satellite communicator (Garmin inReach) for remote SOS messaging when cellular masts fail.
tip: PMR446 channels 1-8 are licence-free across the UK. Agree on a standard call channel and hourly check-in window (e.g. top of the hour) with immediate family.

title: Indoor-safe backup heating and thermal insulation
description: Prepare a designated 'warm room' with heavy curtains, thermal door snakes, 4-season sleeping bags, woollen blankets, and if appropriate, an indoor-safe catalytic gas heater with a working carbon monoxide alarm.
tip: Never use outdoor camping heaters, barbecues, or unvented paraffin stoves inside without proper ventilation; carbon monoxide is odourless and lethal.

title: Outdoor camping gas stove for off-grid hot meals
description: Keep a single-burner butane or propane camping stove with sealed gas canisters stored in a cool place, reserved for boiling water and heating food outdoors or in a well-ventilated porch.
tip: Never operate camping stoves inside sealed domestic rooms. Always store gas cylinders away from heat and direct sunlight.

title: Home maintenance resilience toolkit
description: Assemble emergency repair supplies: pipe insulation foam, self-amalgamating waterproof repair tape, heavy-duty tarpaulin, duct tape, assorted fuses, pry bar, and work gloves.
tip: During winter storms, self-amalgamating tape can temporarily seal burst pipes while mains pressure is isolated.

title: Neighbourhood resilience & vulnerable resident coordination
description: Identify vulnerable neighbours (elderly, mobility-impaired, medically reliant) on your street. Join or establish a local community resilience group linked with your local parish or borough emergency planning officer.
tip: In wide-area crises, community mutual aid resolves over 80% of immediate civilian welfare challenges before statutory emergency services arrive.
